title: Panoramic Stitching Methods for Drones: Rectilinear, 360 Panos, and Post-Processing Workflows

date.basis: Embedded_creation_time metadata indicates 2026-08-21; transcript content references sunrises/sunsets on a single day and multiple drone panoramas, aligning with a production date around this time.

locations.name: Tusk Peak (referenced location in video)
locations.basis: Explicit mention in transcript: “take all of these files from the Tusk, which is that crazy peak that you just saw there. That was at sunrise. This, believe it or not, is sunset from the same exact day.”

summary: The video provides a practical, example-driven tour of drone panorama stitching across several software tools. It explains how lens choice and the number of shots affect field of view, distinguishes rectilinear from spherical (and panometric) stitching, and compares workflows using Lightroom, Photoshop, PTGui Pro, and PanoVolo. Viewers see hands-on demonstrations of wide-angle rectilinear stitching in PTGui Pro, free-panel and 360-degree panoramas, and techniques for handling exposure matching, warping, and edge alignment. The presenter also covers the unique challenges of 360 panos (including look-down limitations and mirroring to fix center alignment) and outlines a practical end-to-end pipeline from initial capture through post-processing to final stitching, including troubleshooting steps when PanoVolo crashes.

sections.title: Intro to panoramic drone stitching and lens field of view
sections.description: Begins with a high-level setup for drone panoramas, noting how different drone cameras yield different effective focal lengths when stitching 9 shots, and introducing the core issue of rectilinear distortion needed to keep horizons straight in wide-angle panoramas.

sections.title: Rectilinear distortion and why it matters
sections.description: Explains why wide-angle rectilinear distortion is used to avoid horizon bending, and contrasts how telephoto and mid-range lenses behave versus wide-angle lenses on stitched panoramas.

sections.title: Overview of stitching tools and options
concepts: differences in exposure handling and stitch types
sections.description: Outlines available stitching ecosystems and their relative strengths, preparing the viewer for deeper demonstrations of specific tools and workflows.

sections.title: Wide-angle pano with PTGui Pro and post-processing
sections.description: Demonstrates opening a set of images in PTGui Pro, selecting rectilinear output, adjusting post-process exposure blending, and preparing the image for final processing with a rectilinear outcome.

sections.title: Free pano and 360 panorama explorations
sections.description: Compares free-panel (DJI) panos to wide-angle panels and previews 360-panorama decisions, including projection choices and how framing affects final output.

sections.title: 360 panorama processing and mirroring technique
sections.description: Goes into depth on the specific challenges of 360 panoramas, including the need to look down to avoid unusable portions, and introduces mirroring as a practical fix for center alignment when stitching results aren’t inherently balanced.

sections.title: Post-processing workflow, troubleshooting, and wrap-up
concepts: stitching with PTGui and Photoshop workflows
sections.description: Wraps up with an end-to-end workflow, detailing batch processing in Lightroom, sequencing in PanoVolo, and stitching in PTGui/Photoshop, plus debugging tips when PanoVolo fails to launch.
